newsitem.title: UK: CU sees UFF purchase earnings enhancing.
newsitem.headline: CU sees UFF purchase earnings enhancing.

text.p: British composite insurer Commercial Union on Tuesday will lift its interest in the French market following an agreement with Credit Agricole Indosuez to purchase a 55.8 percent stake in Union Financiere de France (UFF) for 126 million stg.
CU previously held an 11.7 percent stake in UFF through its French life assurance unit Abeille vie.

UFF, a financial products distribution company listed on the Paris stock exchange, has the largest network of direct sales financial advisers in France with 880 operating from 32 branches servicing 135,000 individual and small company clients.
CU said the acquisition would be effectively financed from Abeille vie's existing resources and expected it to be earnings enhancing.
"We believe the price is a fair one," said CU finance director Peter Foster. Excluding the cash holdings of UFF, CU is paying around 10 times earnings.

The company said the transaction would consolidate the distribution of Abeille vie insurance and savings products. It would also provide additional opportunities to sell investment, pensions and insurance products throughout France, Europe's largest life assurance market.

The impact of the deal on CU's net asset value would be broadly neutral, said Foster. "Given the Abeille link they know the business well and it makes sense to cement the distribution," commented one analyst.
By late afternoon CU shares had dipped 12-1/2 pence to 682 pence.
CU will have to make an offer to minority interests which is likely to result in the company acquiring more of UFF. The exact amount will depend on the take up by minority interests.
The move is in line with Commercial Union's strategy of growing its life business internationally.
Commercial Union acquired Abeille vie in 1994. Last year, 10 percent of Abeille vie's sales were through UFF.
UFF has some 2.3 billion pounds under management and in the year to December 31, 1996 made pre-tax profits of 26 million stg.

Earlier CU reported strong growth in worldwide new business figures. But another drop in French new business amid uncertainty surrounding the recent elections, as well as a reorganisation of the sales force, hit sales.
The French performance was widely expected and further exacerbated by the recent strength of sterling but Foster said France represented a long term strategic investment.
"I think the prospects for France particularly on the life side are extremely good longer term," he said.
